barRaise.topFinding: Skip-unchanged gate fired cleanly for the first time in this series: zero commits since 2026-07-25, working tree byte-identical, no BLOCK. A pure counter-aging carry-forward would have been dishonest today, because the overnight audit found the first defect in the series a user can hit. 43 of 199 herb records carry a descFull longer than the 260-char cap that PROJECT_SPEC.md:43 and data/label-templates.js:70 both assert, range 261 to 317, and src/ui/editor.js:693 autofills with a bare .slice(0, 260) with no word-boundary handling. Re-counted against disk this run. About a fifth of the catalog renders a back label that stops mid-word on a live page, and test-data-integrity.mjs asserts referential integrity but never a character cap. The direction matters: the doc is right and the data violates it, so the usual trust-the-code rule points the wrong way. The second new finding explains why the dashboard never showed it: write-dashboard-status.ps1:171 carries audit.findings forward off the previous JSON instead of parsing the report, so the severity mix has been frozen since it was first written. Offsetting that, two stale queue rows pending on a false claim since 2026-07-17 are gone, so work-queue-hygiene rose 4. Health holds at 83, verdict working, no BLOCK. Three findings chronic at runsOpen 9. Nothing needed auto-enqueueing: all five HIGH/MED ids resolved to live queue rows.

Three stranded edits, main.js at day 12. At runsSeen 3 this is no longer a tradeoff between two good properties; it is a decision nobody has made, and it belongs in adr-promoter as an explicit lock either way.

Word-aware truncation fixes rendering everywhere but ratifies 43 records that violate a documented constraint; raising the cap to 320 honors the content only if the back card holds it at the smallest size, which nobody has measured; trimming honors the constraint but edits deliberate prose. Resolution: measure the 317-char record on the smallest template first, then pick, and make truncation word-aware regardless as a floor.
